purpose: Cabergoline is used to treat conditions caused by too much of a hormone called prolactin in your blood, such as irregular periods, unwanted breast milk, or fertility problems. It is also sometimes used to treat Parkinson's disease. By lowering prolactin levels, it helps your body get back to normal hormonal balance.
how_it_works: Your brain has a chemical messenger called dopamine that normally keeps prolactin levels in check. Cabergoline mimics dopamine by attaching to the same receptors in the brain, which tells your body to slow down prolactin production. Think of it like a key that fits the same lock as dopamine and turns down the signal to make too much prolactin.
common_side_effects: Nausea or upset stomach, headache, dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly), feeling tired, constipation, and stomach pain. These effects are usually mild and often improve after the first few weeks of treatment.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have heart valve problems, high blood pressure, liver disease, or a history of fibrosis (scar tissue buildup in the lungs or heart). Cabergoline can rarely cause compulsive behaviors like gambling or increased sex drive, so let your doctor know if you notice unusual urges. Avoid alcohol. Do not take it if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 0.25 mg (half a tablet) taken twice a week. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over several weeks based on how your body responds, up to a maximum of 1 mg twice a week. It is best taken with food to help reduce stomach upset. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
